# Claim packet 2026-10-15-1

## Problem statement
The van der Waerden number w(2;3,t) is the smallest N such that every 2-colouring of {1,...,N} contains either a
3-term arithmetic progression in colour 0 or a t-term arithmetic progression in colour 1. (An arithmetic progression of
length L means L distinct integers a, a+d, ..., a+(L-1)d with d >= 1, all within {1..N}.)

Published best lower bound for t = 33 (Ahmed, Kullmann, Snevily, "On the van der Waerden numbers w(2;3,t)",
arXiv:1102.5433, Table 3 "Further lower bounds"): w(2;3,33) > 1063.

## Frozen definition of "solved" (written before work started)
An improvement for t = 33 is an explicit 2-colouring of {1, ..., n} with n >= 1064 such that colour 0 contains no 3-term
arithmetic progression and colour 1 contains no 33-term arithmetic progression. Such a colouring proves w(2;3,33) > n.

## Claim
There is a 2-colouring of {1, ..., 1068} with no 3-term AP in colour 0 and no 33-term AP in colour 1.
Hence w(2;3,33) > 1068 (i.e. w(2;3,33) >= 1069), improving the published bound w(2;3,33) > 1063.

## Artifact
The colouring as a string of 1068 characters; the k-th character (k = 1..1068) is the colour of the integer k.
The same string is in `colouring_t33_n1068.txt` in this folder.
